title: A Fish Stayed in the Air for 45 Seconds on Camera

scenes.text: A fish stayed in the air for 45 seconds.
A film crew on a Japanese ferry filmed it in 2008.
The flying fish leaped out, spread its huge side fins, and glided beside the boat.
Most glides last seconds and cover about 160 feet. This one beat the old record of 42 seconds.
The trick is its tail. It keeps dipping it back into the water to paddle itself up again.
All of that effort, just to escape something hungry below.

description:
A fish stayed in the air for 45 seconds.
In 2008 an NHK film crew on a ferry in Japan filmed a flying fish gliding for 45 seconds, a record. Most glides cover about 160 feet.
Would you believe it if you saw it? Tell us below.
first_comment: Typical flying fish glides can reach about 1,300 feet at the very most. Which is crazier, the fish or the camera crew being there?
